title: Quentin and the Will
premise: True-crime podcaster Odile Reyes arrives in the fog-bound town of Marrow's Bend to investigate its coldest case: the 1962 disappearance of a witness named Quentin, whose testimony vanished along with him. When the town founder's coffin is exhumed and found empty, Odile discovers Quentin never died — he was hidden by the very family that founded the town, protected for sixty years by a web of loyalty, guilt, and a will that names him heir. As Odile closes in, they must choose between exposing the truth that will destroy a found family or burying the story forever; in the end, Odile finds Quentin alive, helps him claim his identity on his own terms, and walks away with an unsolved episode — their first — because some cases are meant to be closed by love, not by airtime.
about_author: Oscar Eastwick is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering obituaries before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about the secrets communities keep out of love rather than malice.

chapters.title: The Coldest Case
chapters.summary: Odile Reyes, in their own POV, introduces their podcast and their perfect record of closed cases, then receives an anonymous tip about Marrow's Bend: the founder's coffin, exhumed for a cemetery relocation, is empty. The emotional beat is confident curiosity curdling into unease as Odile realizes the tip came from inside the town.

chapters.title: A Town That Remembers Wrong
chapters.summary: Odile arrives in Marrow's Bend and interviews townsfolk who repeat the official story of 1962 with suspicious uniformity. In the archive, they find a gap where Quentin's testimony should be. POV alternates between Odile and elderly librarian Ruth Halloway, who lies to protect someone. The beat is creeping isolation.

chapters.title: The Will
chapters.summary: Odile obtains the founder Ambrose Vane's will through a sympathetic junior lawyer, Marcus, and discovers a sealed codicil naming an unknown beneficiary. Marcus warns them off. Odile's POV carries the thrill of the hunt; Marcus's interlude reveals his own fear and divided loyalty. The beat is temptation versus warning.

chapters.title: Sixty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV chapter: she remembers 1962, when young Quentin witnessed something in the Vane house and the town chose to hide him rather than hand him over. She tends to a man no one speaks of. The emotional beat is tender, weary devotion — the found family forming around a secret.

chapters.title: Empty Coffin, Full House
chapters.summary: Odile stakes out the abandoned Vane estate and spots fresh footprints, medicine deliveries, and a light in the east wing. Someone confronts them in the dark — a warning, not an attack. Odile's POV; the beat shifts from hunter to hunted as they realize the town protects a living person, not a crime.

chapters.title: What Quentin Saw
chapters.summary: Through recovered letters and Ruth's confession, the 1962 truth emerges: Quentin saw Ambrose's brother commit a killing, and Ambrose staged his own empty grave decades later to keep the secret buried with himself. Odile's POV, interleaved with archival documents. The beat is revelation shadowed by dread — the killer's descendant still lives in town.

chapters.title: The Descendant
chapters.summary: Councilman Everett Vane, learning Odile is close, moves to have the podcast shut down and Ruth evicted. Marcus defects to Odile's side, handing over the codicil. Alternating POV between Odile's fury and Marcus's guilt. The beat is rising stakes: duty to the truth now endangers everyone Odile has come to care for.

chapters.title: Deadline at the Grave
chapters.summary: Everett digs up the empty grave site himself to force a scandal that will flush Quentin out. Odile races him to the estate. The confrontation turns violent when Everett, cornered, admits what his grandfather did. Odile's POV; the beat is fear and resolve colliding at the climax's edge.

chapters.title: Quentin
chapters.summary: Climax: Odile finally meets Quentin — old, sharp, and furious at being found. He refuses rescue but accepts choice: with Ruth, Marcus, and Odile standing witness, he signs the codicil, claims his name publicly, and lets Everett's confession go to the sheriff. The beat is catharsis; identity reclaimed not as exposure but as homecoming.

chapters.title: An Unsolved Episode
chapters.summary: Resolution: Odile records a final episode that tells everything except Quentin's location, closing the series with their first deliberately unfinished case. Ruth and Marcus see them off; Quentin sends a letter that begins a friendship. The beat is bittersweet peace — love against duty, resolved in favor of both.
